title: Learning Low-Latency Action Verification for Frozen Vision-Language-Action Models
why: A-type action-verification harness around a frozen VLA: hindsight from the policy's own rollouts trains a compact success-score verifier that selects among action-chunk candidates at execution time, with LIBERO-10 and real-world manipulation results.
mechanism: HDH has three stages. The frozen VLA is first deployed to collect autonomous rollouts. A compact action verifier is then trained to assign each action chunk a predicted task-success score. At execution, the frozen VLA generates action candidates and the verifier selects the highest-scoring candidate. The design targets the latency of computationally expensive verifiers at each policy query.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on four LIBERO-10 tasks, HDH records an average success rate of 82.3%. On three real-world manipulation tasks, it improves average success over the baseline policy by 22.6%. Numeric tables and baselines beyond the abstract unread.

title: Decide Before You Move: Diffusion-Generated Search Reference for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Object Navigation in Semi-Static Environments
why: A-type ObjectNav harness (PreNav) that calls an LLM once, before motion, to turn a target–furniture co-occurrence prior into a spatial search reference, instead of invoking a VLM at every step, then executes along a diffusion-generated centerline in semi-static scenes.
mechanism: PreNav keeps a map of walls and large furniture for path planning and uses a target–furniture co-occurrence prior for where to search. An LLM converts that prior into a spatial prior; a conditional diffusion model turns the prior plus persistent structure into an ordered centerline with a band around it. The robot approaches the target once it is detected online, rather than re-deriving where to look with a vision-language model every few steps.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on a Gibson ObjectNav benchmark, PreNav outperforms a strong online baseline under matched structural priors. The generator is trained only on room-level ScanNet++ scenes and applied to floor-level Gibson without fine-tuning. Real-world experiments under object relocation and open-vocabulary queries are also reported. Numeric tables beyond the abstract unread.

title: BiPOP: Partial-Order Planning for Long-Horizon Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
why: A-type bimanual planning harness: an LLM translates natural-language instructions into PDDL, and a temporal partial-order planner enforces reachability, synchronization, and concurrent-execution constraints; evaluated in simulation and run on the real bimanual robot NICOL.
mechanism: BiPOP couples an LLM with Temporal Partial-Order Planning. An explicit spatio-temporal model partitions the workspace by arm reachability and captures inter-arm dependencies, arm assignment, synchronization, and safe concurrency. The LLM writes a formal PDDL specification from the instruction; a temporal planner enforces those constraints and schedules actions, aiming for symbolically consistent plans that can execute in parallel.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on simulated long-horizon tasks of varying complexity, BiPOP outperforms open-loop planning with strong reasoning models and closed-loop ReAct-style planning in success rate, planning time, and plan efficiency. The full pipeline is reported to run end to end on the real bimanual robot NICOL. A failure analysis attributes LLM-only planners' errors mainly to spatial and temporal coordination-constraint violations. Numeric tables beyond the abstract unread.

title: What Makes a VLA Reactive? A Study of Execution Strategies for Dynamic Manipulation
why: B-type execution-control study of what makes a pretrained VLA reactive on dynamic manipulation: it varies prediction/execution horizons, synchronous vs asynchronous inference, continuity-preserving execution, and limited policy adaptation, arguing that the execution pipeline should be evaluated together with the policy.
mechanism: The study uses a pretrained VLA on two dynamic simulation benchmarks and three real-robot tasks. It varies prediction and execution horizons, compares synchronous and asynchronous inference, tests methods that deliver actions sooner or keep successive chunks continuous, and adapts the policy with motion cues and latent-space reinforcement learning. The authors report that the best prediction horizon is about one second, that the best execution horizon depends on the checkpoint, that short horizons help more with asynchronous execution, and that methods keeping the trajectory continuous outperform those that only reduce latency.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): qualitative and comparative findings on two dynamic simulation benchmarks and three real-robot tasks, including a conveyor task where changing the execution horizon gained as much as targeted policy adaptation. No single headline success rate is given in the abstract. Numeric tables unread.

title: Recover, Don't Just Continue: Learning from Feedback for Physical Failure Understanding and Correction
why: A-type failure-understanding and corrective-planning harness (Embodied-Corrector) that localizes causal failures, adapts under capability constraints, and revises plans from interaction; deployed with a frozen VLA or with fixed GPT-5.5 execution on manipulation and navigation tasks.
mechanism: Embodied-Corrector constructs failure-recovery data by injecting perturbations at subtask boundaries of successful trajectories, replaying affected subtasks, and keeping failures that are observable and recoverable. Actions, consequences, failure causes, and recoveries are aligned into Judge-Cause-Sub-Fine supervision. Training is evaluation-first SFT (Judge and Cause first, then Sub and Fine), then OPD so the model internalizes planning under self-generated prefixes; the contrastive prefix branch is removed at deployment.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): with a frozen VLA, composite task success improves by 6.1 percentage points; with fixed GPT-5.5 execution, manipulation and navigation tasks improve by 13.9 percentage points. Benchmark names and raw trial counts are not stated in the abstract. Numeric tables unread.

title: COMBS: Concealed Object Multi-modal Bayesian Search
why: A-type concealed-object search harness (COMBS) that fuses ontology, semantic-network, LLM, and VLM priors into a Bayes-adaptive mixed-observability planner, compared against a per-step LLM policy in simulation including Matterport3D with a real detector.
mechanism: COMBS uses a concealment-adaptive mixed-observability MDP (CA-MOMDP) in which uncertainty is over both object locations and which nodes can conceal them. A hierarchical transition system abstracts the environment into room and object nodes. A COMBS-score fuses a human-informed semantic network, an LLM, and a VLM to initialize the location belief; belief is updated by Bayes' rule and looking never rules out a closed container. The method can declare a target absent at a stated error level.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): across five simulator configurations, from a gridworld to Matterport3D with a real detector, COMBS finds 92–100% of in-distribution and 92–100% of out-of-distribution targets, matches or beats baselines in processing speed, and significantly outperforms a per-step LLM policy at lower cost on larger scenes. When the per-step LLM policy is offered a termination action it abandons 12–22% of present targets, versus 1.6–3.2% for COMBS. It also recovers more out-of-distribution placements than a TidyBot ranking. Numeric tables beyond the abstract unread.

title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
why: B-type controlled study of GPT-6 robot-use agents that isolates harness, action interface, experience reuse, and scene-geometry choices in one framework; a lean harness starting from an official L3 design raises RoboDojo simulation scores substantially without a learned policy or self-improvement loop.
mechanism: JustRUA holds the model fixed and varies the harness around it, the action interface, reuse of experience, and the scene geometry given to the model. The authors report that a lean harness that keeps the full episode history and stops each motion early goes a long way; experience reuse changes how the model acts but is not a free lunch; and scene geometry helps most, even when depth is predicted from RGB alone. The recommended recipe starts from the official L3 harness and keeps only what matters most.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): even with no learned policy, self-improvement loop, or task-specific tuning, the simple harness raises the score on the RoboDojo simulation benchmark from 29.7 to 50.3. Other reported robot-use agents are described as hard to compare because they differ in harness and test subset. Numeric tables beyond the abstract unread.

title: What Can a VLA Learn from the Agent That Calls It? Task-Level Experience Distillation for Embodied Navigation
why: A-type harness distillation (H2E): successful sessions of an LLM-planner agent that calls a VLA, including tool-driven motions and detours, are converted into task-level VLA training data so the VLA can navigate alone at test time on REVERIE-CE.
mechanism: Navigation agents use an LLM planner to call a VLA, which is costly per episode. H2E distills successful agent experience into the VLA rather than distilling the planner. Every motion becomes a VLA action under the original task instruction, with resulting poses as targets. The loss is masked on steps that move away from the goal, and every visited state within 1 m of the goal is labeled as a stop. The VLA is then updated with low-rank adaptation and, at test time, navigates alone.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on all 3,189 REVERIE-CE val-unseen episodes, H2E raises the success rate of an 8B VLA from 35.0% to 44.9%. The VLA is reported to learn to stop at the goal and to find goals the base model never reaches. Numeric tables beyond the abstract unread.

title: HeMeR: Heterogeneous Memory Reconciliation for Embodied Agents via Structured KV Reuse
why: A-type memory-harness inference layer (HeMeR) that reconciles declarative, procedural, and working memory for embodied agents via structured KV-cache reuse as memory contents change during interaction, evaluated on ALFWorld, Habitat, and real-world robot deployments.
mechanism: Embodied agents combine heterogeneous memory modules, but existing modules are typically accessed through separate interfaces, forcing full KV recomputation even when much of the memory context is unchanged. HeMeR tracks declarative, procedural, and working memory across action decisions, preserves KV states for unchanged contents, and reconciles only the KV states affected by updates, so inference can stay efficient as memory evolves.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): evaluated on ALFWorld, Habitat, and real-world robotic deployments requiring coordinated use of heterogeneous memory. In the real-world setting, HeMeR achieves 83.20% task success and reduces per-step inference time from 2.94 to 1.87 seconds compared with MemRL, while preserving compatible KV states as task progress updates the memory context. title: Reins: Frontier Multimodal Models Driving Real Robot Arms on Long-Horizon Tasks, Zero-Shot
why: A-type robot-use harness (Reins) in which an off-the-shelf frontier multimodal model operates a dual-arm robot with 3D perception tools and contact/grip-reporting atomic actions, plus a narrator instance and a simulation-ready scene twin; compared with and without the harness on five real long-horizon tasks. Distinct from corpus REINS 2611.10748.
mechanism: Reins is a harness in which an off-the-shelf model operates a dual-arm robot with 3D perception tools and atomic actions that report contact and grip. The model can chain actions in one call, each with a condition that must hold, stopping at the first that fails. A second instance, the narrator, watches the cameras continuously and reports what changed with every result. From images, Reins also builds a simulation-ready twin of the scene for continual policy learning. No task-specific code is used; prompts are natural language. The paper notes the model is otherwise blind while the arm moves and while it thinks.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): with natural-language prompts and no task-specific code, GPT-6.1 Sol succeeds in 88% of real episodes on five tasks; without the harness, it fails every shell game and takes 8 times as long. Three frontier models are reported to perform alike but to differ in tracking a scene that changes while the actor thinks. Trial counts per task are not stated in the abstract. Numeric tables unread.

title: NSDL: Neuro-Symbolic Division of Labor for Multi-Robot Task Planning
why: A-type neuro-symbolic multi-robot planning harness (NSDL): a small VLM writes a plan sketch (goals still needing action and intended robot-assigned steps) using a detector tool, and a deterministic solver expands the sketch into an executable joint plan, with the solver in the training loop.
mechanism: NSDL splits two kinds of decisions. A small vision-language model judges from the scene which goals are already met, how the task splits, and which robot does what, and calls a detector for evidence. A deterministic solver computes prerequisite actions, handoffs, and timing. The model writes a plan sketch that lists remaining goals and intended steps with a robot; the solver expands the sketch into an executable joint plan. The model is trained with the solver in the loop.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): evaluated on the public VIKI-L2 benchmark and on a new LOCUS-Bench that grades the two kinds of difficulty separately. NSDL outperforms end-to-end planners and formalize-then-plan baselines on both benchmarks and with three backbones from 3B to 8B; the 7B model reaches 97.0% out-of-distribution accuracy on VIKI-L2. Ordering and scheduling errors are reported to nearly disappear once the solver writes the structure; remaining failures are misjudged states. Numeric tables beyond the abstract unread.

title: ACE-CaP-0: Real-World Code-as-Policies in the Era of Experience
why: A-type real-world Code-as-Policies recipe (ACE-CaP-0): a coding agent revises executable robot programs using demonstrations on request and simulation on demand, then leaves frozen programs to run with runtime perception and control and no human or coding agent in the loop.
mechanism: ACE-CaP-0 is an agentic recipe that couples policy revision with experience acquisition through Demonstrations on Request and Simulation on Demand. The authors investigate human guidance as a source of priors for feasible actions and simulation as an auxiliary environment for exploring and testing candidate policies; they report favoring on-request robot demonstrations and selective use of simulation during real-world policy refinement. The resulting programs execute with runtime perception and control, without a human or coding agent in the loop, so reasoning invested in development can be reused across runs.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): across eight real-world manipulation tasks spanning alignment, multi-object handling, and bimanual coordination, the frozen programs achieve 92.1% success (221/240 trials). Mean execution times across tasks range from 0.97 to 2.27 minutes. Numeric tables beyond the abstract unread.
